rationale:
Evidence: the best raced design is iteration 8 (kd 1.1, base 1.5, kp 3.5, ki 0.05, weights [1, 0.5, 0, -0.5, -1], 12 mm sensors at y=0.06, last_direction). It scored 395.348. The oval finished 20 of 20 with steering_oscillation 0.217. The s-bend and slalom failed in every trial, and they account for almost all of the remaining score headroom. The authorized entity0 draft (kd 2.5, base 1.2, y=0.04) does not match the raced 395.3 design, so I do not build from it.

Critique handling:
(1) Accepted: the revision is identical to the raced design, so I do not treat it as a new hypothesis. I keep it unchanged.
(2) Partly accepted: re-racing an unchanged design gives little new information. I still keep it, because the final score is measured on an unseen track, and a design with a measured 20-of-20 oval finish and a known score is the lowest-risk submission. Any change to kd, speed or sensor layout could break the oval finish, which carries about 950 points of the mean.
(3) Accepted in part: the s-bend progress fell from 0.424 at kd 0.8 to 0.395 at kd 1.1, so the s-bend optimum may sit below 1.1. I do not act on this, because kd 0.8 has a lower oval finish rate (14 of 20) and kd 1.1 is the only setting with a clean oval finish.
(4) Rejected: the claim that slalom is flat above kd 0.8 has no measured support at 1.4 or 1.8. I do not predict a slalom gain. Slalom progress is 0.178 here, the same as at kd 0.8 within noise.
(5) Rejected: the decision rule to test kd 1.4 is hard to trigger, as the critique notes. I replace it with a clearer rule below.

Decision rule for the next revision: if the oval finish rate falls below 0.6 or steering_oscillation exceeds 0.40, revert to kd 0.8. Otherwise, test one change at a time on the s-bend, starting with a small kd reduction to 0.9 or 1.0, and keep the oval finish as the gate.

Expected result: score near 395, with oval finish 1.0 and steering_oscillation near 0.22. No s-bend or slalom gain is predicted.
